text: Is your AI missing the mark? Do you keep reminding it which pattern to follow, and what not to do?
There are usually two reasons. The AI drifts, and you go round in correction loops. Or the ask is thin, so it fills the gaps with guesses.
Sensei reads your sessions. Every follow-up that corrects the AI's work, like “that's not what I asked” or “revert that”, is a signal. And it tracks which sessions land first time.
When the same correction keeps coming back, Sensei turns it into a rule. The AI loads those rules at the start of the next session, so you don't have to say it again.
For thin asks, Sensei checks the plan before work starts: clear acceptance criteria, defined inputs, no open questions. Then an adversarial review hunts for what was missed.
Every change is measured. If a rule helps, more sessions land first time, and it stays. If it doesn't, you'll see that too.
